title: Pandolfo Malatesta, archbishop of Patras (Rome), to Gianfrancesco Gonzaga, 22 Apr 1428, Archivio di Stato di Mantova (DECODE R1854 image 1)

documents.shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Mantova, Archivio Gonzaga (busta not given on DECODE), DECODE R1854 image 1

transcription.source: DECODE images via saved session cookie
transcription.notes: First pass by the model, second pass sign by sign by a subagent (p1v2.txt): 262 signs in 3 runs.

system.summary: Three cipher runs of letter-like signs in a clear Latin letter; system not identified (not a simple or homophonic substitution in Latin or Italian).
system.sibling_key: None fits: the R1853 register's Malatesta keys (1406-19), R1855 (Este keys incl. Malatesta Novello 1441) and R1852 (Florence Dieci 1424-32) tried.
system.notes: IC 0.056 with 29 sign types and about 44% vowel-like signs. Separators strewn between signs. Split 14 Oct 2026 from r1854.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: DECODE login cookie and /goal target setting. No target-specific intervention.

solution.what: Fetched R1854 (5 images), the R1853 register (14 images) and DECODE metadata with the saved cookie.
Web search for Pandolfo Malatesta's ciphered letters (Treccani DBI; Falcioni 2015 prints the plaintext of his 1438 cipher letter, ASMn AG b. 1081).
Read the R1853 register keys (Malatesta keys on f. 1, 1406-1419 keys): none match the 1428-30 letters.
Opened all other Mantova records on DECODE (R7858-R7888): 16th-17th century keys.
P1 anneals in Latin and Italian, with and without spaces, costed nulls, vowel constraint, reversed orders, split and merged digraphs: no reading.
Solver reads a synthetic 266-letter monoalphabetic Latin text, also with 12% token noise: P1 is not a simple substitution in Latin.
Register key 'cum Malatesta dni Pandulfi' values seeded into the P1 anneal: -4.2/char, no fit.
Subagent second pass of P1 (262 signs, 3 runs, 3 misreadings fixed) and clear-text transcription.
P1 re-solved from the second pass in Latin, Italian and modern Italian: no reading.

P1: digraphic test (sign-pair IC 0.005, no), periodicity test (column IC flat for periods 2-8, not polyalphabetic), vowel/consonant alternation 0.713 above all 200 shuffles (linear text, not transposed).
P1 annealed in Spanish, Catalan, French, German, Portuguese, and with order-3 Latin/Italian models over 150 restarts: no reading.
Opened DECODE R1855 (Modena Este keys, incl. Malatesta Novello 1441) and R1852 (Florence Dieci keys 1424-32): sign sets differ from P1, no fit.
P1 syllable-aware anneal (each sign a letter, one of 27 common Latin/Italian syllables or word signs, or null; frequency prior): no reading.
Images re-fetched from DECODE with the saved cookie (PNG, P1 1121x697 px); P1 run lines cropped at 3x, L05 matches p1v2.txt sign for sign.

P1 annealed with the separators kept as cipher signs (// : ... . | as five extra signs, p1_withsep.txt), Latin and Italian, 10 restarts each: best -2.76 (la) and -2.63 (it-cinquecento) per char, no words; separators are not hidden letters.
Split from the R1854 entry under the one-key rule (Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): the record's four letters use four ciphers; image 1 is this entry, not solved.

outcome.method_basis: Annealing under twelve hypotheses (Latin, Italian, other Romance and German models, costed nulls, vowel classes, reversals, digraph splits, syllable signs, separators as signs) gave no reading, while the same solver reads a synthetic text of this length with 12% noise; no register or sibling key fits.

gaps.detail: not a simple or homophonic substitution in Latin or Italian; none of the register's Malatesta keys fits; the likely key material is Pandolfo's ciphered letter of 1 Mar 1438 with its contemporary translation (ASMn AG b. 1081 c. 159-160 and b. 840 c. 95, Falcioni 2015), whose ciphertext is not online and not printed

outcome.notes: Split 14 Oct 2026 from the four-letter R1854 entry; catalogue entry 152.
